::: {.entry-meta}
[new component]{.chip .built} Entry 64 · milestone JOREK (alongside M4)
:::

To use JOREK as a reference, the toolkit has to write JOREK inputs from its own
equilibria and profiles, read JOREK's outputs, and run cases with a full record of what
was executed. These parts are now in place as open (Tier A) code that runs without
JOREK installed.

The design choice that mattered is what the adapter does not do. JOREK's own
conversion scripts mix unit conversion with physics choices: how profiles continue
outside the separatrix, a default diffusivity, Spitzer resistivity, grid sizes. The
toolkit adapter only converts units and writes files. Every physics setting is an
explicit input from the caller, with no default, so each one is visible and goes to
the owner for a decision.

The adapter converts to JOREK's normalised units using the constants of the pinned
JOREK version. Checked against the units JOREK itself stored in three restart files,
the conversion agrees to round-off ([time and resistivity units computed by the toolkit match the values JOREK stored in three restart files to 1e-15 relative]{.claim}[C-213](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-213){.cid .st-tested}). The namelist writer was
tested against the real program. A MAST-U input parsed and rewritten by the toolkit
gives a restart file identical to the original input's ([the MAST-U input (356 entries) parsed and rewritten by the toolkit gives, with one thread, a restart file identical in every dataset to a run of the original input]{.claim}[C-214](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-214){.cid .st-measured}). This
check is independent of our code, because JOREK parses the file.

The same test exposed a property of JOREK we had to account for. Runs with more than
one OpenMP thread are not bitwise repeatable, and they intermittently abort during grid
set-up ([an assertion in the element search tree aborts 3 of 8 grid set-up runs at 8 OpenMP threads and 0 of 8 at 1 thread; two 4-thread runs of the same input differ at round-off, while 1-thread runs repeat bit for bit]{.claim}[C-212](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-212){.cid .st-measured}). The run wrapper therefore does three things:
- it records ranks and threads, and marks a run as bitwise repeatable only at one thread;
- it retries the grid-set-up abort once, and only when no time step has completed;
- it keeps every attempt.

The wrapper snapshots the executable and inputs read-only and writes a provenance
record beside every file. Its tests use fake executables ([26 tests pass in normal and Tier-A-only modes: unit conversion, profile files, namelists, the energy reader, and the runner with fake executables (snapshots, retry, timeout, provenance)]{.claim}[C-215](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-215){.cid .st-tested}). On the
real program it reproduces a manual run exactly.

Where this stands: adapter and wrapper done; the abort is to be reported to the JOREK
developers.
